claims.text: Deviating from equiatomic elemental ratios can tune magnetic ordering temperatures in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Deviating from equiatomic elemental ratios can tune magnetocaloric effects in non-equiatomic HEAs.
A non-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA can retain a single-phase solid-solution structure.
Changing elemental concentrations changes the local atomic configuration.
Compositional variation modifies the proximity among magnetic atoms.
Compositional variation modifies the interaction strength among magnetic atoms.
Adjusting composition changes the strength and nature of magnetic exchange interactions.
Adjusting composition changes the distribution of magnetic moments.
Changes in exchange interactions and magnetic moments shift magnetic phase-transition temperatures.
Changes in exchange interactions and magnetic moments alter the magnetic entropy change.
The magnetic entropy change is closely related to the nature of the magnetic transition.
Co is a magnetic species with a sizable magnetic moment in CoCrFeMnNi.
Fe is a strongly magnetic species in the proposed CoCrFeMnNi-based alloy.
Increasing the concentration of strongly magnetic species raises the magnetic ordering temperature.
Increasing the concentration of strongly magnetic species enhances the magnetic entropy change.
Increasing the concentration of strongly magnetic species improves magnetocaloric performance.
Excessive compositional deviation may cause phase separation.
Excessive compositional deviation may reduce microstructural homogeneity.
Loss of the desired single-phase structure compromises magnetocaloric properties.
Composition tuning is beneficial only within a finite compositional window.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that excessive compositional deviation may destroy the single-phase structure and eliminate magnetocaloric benefits, but the falsification rule treats loss of the single-phase structure without magnetocaloric tuning as falsifying the hypothesis. That observation would instead be consistent with the stated boundary condition unless it occurred inside a predefined beneficial composition window.
